sections.html: Tenellus leporhinus (formerly Nemadoras leporhinus) is a medium-sized thorny catfish that reaches a standard length of around 8 cm (excluding caudal fin).

The thorny catfishes of the genera Doras, Hassar, Hemidoras, Leptodoras, Nemadoras and Tenellus look quite similar at first glimpse and have often been confused with each other in the past, both in scientific and aquarium literature; accordingly, there are always small question marks behind the identification of rarely imported species.

Juveniles (3-5 cm) from Colombia are identified as Tenellus leporhinus on the basis of the shape of the head and the pattern of the dorsal fin spine.
As far as care is concerned, all the basic rules for keeping Corydoras catfish apply.

The juveniles are extremely lively and highly active and are great fun to watch. Adult Tenellus are more active at dusk. They should always be kept in shoals, as they always seek the company of conspecifics. They are completely peaceful towards other fish and pay no attention to plants.
